text:
Tyler Boucher waited a long time for Tuesday. The 10th pick in 2021 made his NHL debut in Winnipeg and scored the winner, with his father, Brian, the former NHL goalie, watching; Graeme Nichols of Coming Down the Pipe noted he joined Carter Yakemchuk as the only Ottawa first-rounders to score in a debut with the club. Viggo Björck got his first one too, and the Senators ended the Jets' six-game winning streak. That is three straight wins and 4-0-1 in five for Ottawa, now at an 89% playoff chance in our simulations.

The run isn't a fluke. Ottawa took 59% of the expected goals (the quality of the chances) in the three wins, and over the season holds 53% at five on five. Then there's Linus Ullmark: a .940 save percentage and 10.3 goals saved above expected in 11 games, a year after he finished at -13.3. He is projected again tonight. The Senators are doing it shorthanded, too, with William Eklund on injured reserve until about Jan. 5; Tim Stützle has moved beside Dylan Cozens and Fabian Zetterlund in his place.

Philadelphia arrives 3-1-1 in five with 57% of the chances in those games, which is a real change from a season at 44% at five on five. The Flyers have also finished 11.2 goals below what their chances usually produce. The noise is around Matvei Michkov, whose future has become trade-rumor material (Rick Tocchet told PhillyVoice the team has handled it "really well" but that it's there). Michkov's answer so far is a five-game point streak. Travis Konecny is pointless in four on 2.7 expected goals, so the looks are coming. Dan Vladar, at -3.2 this season after a strong 2025-26, is projected in net even though Joseph Woll has won three straight starts.

These teams have split two meetings, each winning once on the other's chances. Our model has Ottawa ahead in expected goals tonight, 3.17 to 2.56. Oliver Bonk, born in Ottawa, plays at home for the Flyers.
headline: Boucher's big night and a hot Ottawa
